summary: Exploring the Earth is an interactive, audio-first web application prototype designed to help blind and visually impaired users independently explore Earth observation and NASA climate data.  Most platforms that share environmental and satellite data rely almost entirely on visual maps, charts, and images, creating a major barrier for people with vision loss. Our solution bridges this accessibility gap by turning raw NASA climate data—such as temperature shifts, wind patterns, and terrain features—into an engaging auditory experience.  Using full screen-reader support and AI voice navigation, users can explore environmental changes across two contrasting regions, East Africa and Northern Europe, along an interactive timeline from 2000 to 2026. When a user selects a specific location, a calm AI narrator tells the story of that environment like a documentary, supported by dynamic 3D spatial soundscapes—such as coastal breezes or directional wind audio that shifts between left and right headphones based on real data. This matters because it makes Earth science inclusive, allowing blind and low-vision learners to genuinely experience and understand how our planet is changing.
details:
1. What it does :

Exploring the Earth is an interactive, audio-first web application prototype designed to bridge the accessibility gap for blind and visually impaired users. It transforms raw NASA Earth observation and climate data—such as surface temperature anomalies, wind vectors, and regional topography—into an engaging, cinema-grade auditory experience. Focusing on two pilot regions, East Africa and Northern Europe, the platform allows users to explore multi-decade environmental changes across a chronological timeline from 2000 to 2026 (in 5-year intervals up to 2025, plus 2026).

​2. How it works :

​AI Voice Navigation & Authentication: Users log in securely via screen-reader compatibility and interact with a voice assistant that confirms spoken commands and guides them seamlessly to their regional hub.

​Auditory Timeline & Topography Discovery: Users navigate the 2000–2026 timeline through dynamic screen-reader voice prompts, select a target year, and browse an accessible list of regional terrains—culminating in an option for a Full Location Audio Tour.

​Cinematic Storytelling & Spatial Audio Engine: Upon selecting a specific terrain, a soothing AI narrative describes NASA climate metrics like a documentary. Behind the story, the Web Audio API (StereoPannerNode) renders dynamic spatial soundscapes where environmental sounds (such as wind or coastal breezes) shift their stereo pan between left and right headphones based on real directional data vectors.

​3. Benfits & What we Hope to Achieve :

​Inclusivity & Empowerment: Democratizes scientific discovery, ensuring that the over 2.2 billion people globally with vision impairment are not excluded from exploring planetary science.

​Cognitive Immersion: Replaces dry, fragmented numerical metadata with emotionally resonant storytelling and spatial immersion, transforming passive accessibility compliance into an intuitive educational tool.

​4. Toools, Technologies & Hardware / software used :

​Frontend Architecture: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript / React (WCAG AAA and WAI-ARIA compliant design for screen readers and keyboard navigation).

​Audio Engineering: Web Audio API (AudioContext, StereoPannerNode) for 3D spatial sound panning and dynamic ambient soundscape generation.

​Voice & AI Pipeline: Web Speech API (SpeechRecognition & SpeechSynthesis) combined with LLM-driven narrative storytelling templates.

​Data Sources: NASA Earth Observing System Data and Information System (EOSDIS) / Giovanni surface temperature and wind datasets (2000–2026), and NASA POWER API.

​5. Main use case, Date support & Limitations :

​Main Use Case: Enabling a blind student or curious learner to independently "hear" and experience how climate change has shaped East Africa or Northern Europe over the last 26 years.

​Data Support: Longitudinal NASA meteorological and topographical datasets directly drive the narrative tone, temperature shifts, and stereo wind panning.

​Current Limitations (Prototype Scope): Currently limited to two pilot regions (East Africa and Northern Europe) and pre-curated checkpoint years rather than real-time live streaming of all global satellite feeds.

​Future Scalability: Expanding global regional coverage, converting the web prototype into a fully native mobile application, and integrating live NASA telemetry APIs.
